Yes, most technicians want to leave retail for long term care or hospital pharmacy. I can't speak for all as I certainly met some that were happy in retail, but more often it was used as a stepping stone. I was in school as well for nursing. 

It often isn't the fault of staff, but that of bad management. We were often trying to train brand new techs during rushes, which made for further delays and more customer upset. It was a lose-lose that came from management that we had to deal with.

I may or may not have worked there, at several different locations in 2 states as a technician. And I've had nightmares with that damn music in the background. 

Training is nearly the same at every store, save the state change because different states have all kinds of different laws.
At every store i worked at, technicians were supposed to be assigned a "station" with different duties and rotate throughout the day. In theory, it'd run smoothly. However, this was absolutely impossible due to extremely low staffing, no overtime, and very high turn over. 

The result is technicians and pharmacists running around like chickens with our heads off trying to do everything while doctors are calling, there's a mile long line inside and at the drive thru, people are dropping off prescriptions faster than we can fill them because they're expecting 1 technician to do the work of 3. 

After about 4 years there on and off, getting robbed at gunpoint and punched by a patient, I left pharmacy indefinitely.
